text:
oncall-bot: P1 alert triggered — dedicated pool dedpool-24 node gpu-node-12 reported thermal_trip and auto-drain started. Impact: HydraHealth (dedicated tenant) showing elevated 5xx rate and reduced throughput. Paging alex (oncall). Metrics: GPU temp > 92C, fan rpm at max, nvml reports ECC errors.

alex: acknowledging. I’m on it. First pass: check node health and active sessions.

alex: running `ssh gpu-node-12` — node reachable but `nvidia-smi` shows GPUs offline. Starting `kubectl get pods -n dedpool-24 -o wide` to see evictions.

ops-bot: evict-controller initiated drain for node gpu-node-12: pods gracefully terminating, 30s grace. Eviction reason: thermal_trip.

maria: quick note — HydraHealth is on a VPC-dedicated pool with strict tenant isolation. We need to avoid cross-tenant migration into their VPC. If we move HydraHealth pods, do it to their warm spare nodes only (dedpool-24-warm-01/02). @support_sara loop in CS for customer comms.

support_sara: pinging HydraHealth account lead via email/SMS now. I’ll say we see degraded service and we are executing failover to warm spare; will provide ETA after SRE confirms drain completion.

alex: pod list snapshot (excerpt):
```
NAMESPACE     NAME                          READY   STATUS        NODE          RESTARTS
hydra-health  hydra-api-5f8b7c9d6f-xyz12   0/1     Terminating   gpu-node-12   0
hydra-health  hydra-worker-0               0/1     Terminating   gpu-node-12   0
```
`kubectl describe node gpu-node-12` shows kernel OOM? No, thermal sensor tripped. NVML: GPU 0 ECC errors increasing.

eng_liz: if thermal hardware fault confirmed, we should mark node as unschedulable and provision replacement hardware. Can we keep HydraHealth on their warm spares while node is RMA? Also confirm if dedicated pool has pre-warmed spare capacity.

alex: marking node cordoned: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` then `rwctl drain --node gpu-node-12 --force --tenant hydra-health`. Drain progress currently 60%.

maria: checking capacity — warm spare dedpool-24-warm-01 has 1 free GPU slot; warm-02 has 2. We can shift HydraHealth traffic gradually. Suggest rate-limited rescheduling to avoid overloading network.

jamal: I’ll take over deep-dive if this crosses my shift boundary at 03:00. Plan to handoff at 02:50 with status update.

alex: drain complete for hydra-health pods. Running health probes against hydra endpoints on warm spares. Preliminary: latency returned to baseline for GET /v1/infer, errors dropped from 18% -> 0.8%.

ops-bot: routing update applied — traffic split 0.0 -> 100% to dedpool-24-warm-01/02 for hydra-health. Route id: route-ded24-hh-2026-03-15.

support_sara: updated HydraHealth PM: we’ve failed over your workload to warm spare nodes within your dedicated pool, errors resolved for most requests. We are replacing the failed GPU node and will share timeline for full capacity restore. Customer asked about data paths — confirmed no cross-tenant shared disks were used; isolation preserved.

alex: opening a hardware ticket with vendor — ticket #HW-54219, request priority RMA A100 card + thermal sensor replacement. Also filing internal post-incident task to review cooling profile for dedpool-24 rack B.

maria: mitigation checklist: 1) node cordoned/drained (done) 2) traffic routed to warm spares (done) 3) customer notified (done) 4) hardware RMA open (done) 5) monitor for regressions for 2 hours (in progress) 6) schedule oncall handoff (pending).

eng_liz: confirm we should not evict any other tenants into HydraHealth VPC. Confirmed — keep isolation. Also QA wants to run a small eval job on warm spare to validate model consistency once fully stable.

alex: monitoring shows stable CPU/GPU utilization on warm spares ~65%, latency 120ms p95, error rate <1%. I’ll hand this to @jamal at 02:50 for overnight watch and vendor follow-up.

jamal: taking over. Will re-check hardware ticket status and temperature logs. If vendor ETA slips beyond 4 hours, we’ll spin up an extra warm node in the region (approval from ops). Will update every 30 mins.

sre_lead: good job triaging. Action items assigned: ops to track RMA, eng to validate model quality on warm spare, support to keep customer updates, oncall to watch for regressions. Postmortem owner: maria. 

alex: leaving notes in incident board and runbooks. Handing off now to jamal. :handshake:

jamal: acknowledged. Handoff timestamp: 1772003680. Continuing monitoring — will escalate to ops if any increase in 5xx or thermal alarms on other nodes.

ops-bot: auto-check scheduled: every 5 minutes for next 2 hours on dedpool-24 and warm spares. Logs will be archived to incident-1772003456.

maria: expected next steps: vendor RMA within 6 hours, hardware replacement verification, follow-up postmortem with mitigation to avoid thermal trips (rack cooling review, GPU firmware update).
